jobDescription: The bottling plant runs three high-speed lines on a three-shift pattern. The Shift Operations Supervisor runs a shift across the three lines: allocates the crew to the lines, runs the shift start and hand-over briefings, resolves line stoppages with the maintenance technician, records the shift's output and downtime, and documents the shift's open items. Line speed and product changeover decisions stay with the production manager. The role requires giving clear briefings to a crew of eighteen at shift start. Reports to the production manager; works with the shift crews, the maintenance technicians and the quality inspectors.
requirements: Allocates the shift crew across the three lines under the crewing plan.
Runs the shift start and hand-over briefings for the crew under the briefing standard.
Resolves line stoppages with the maintenance technician under the stoppage procedure.
Records the shift's output and downtime, with line speed and changeover decisions staying with the production manager, and records own responsibility boundaries.
Documents the shift's open items and hand-over conditions.

evidence.text: Shift operations supervisor at a bottling plant with three high-speed lines for four years, allocating a crew of seventeen across the lines each shift under the plant's crewing plan.
Ran the shift start and hand-over briefings under the plant's briefing standard, with the briefing records signed by the crew leads each shift and audited monthly by the production manager.
Resolved the line stoppages with the shift maintenance technician under the stoppage procedure, with each stoppage and its resolution logged in the line system.
Recorded the shift's output and downtime in the line system each shift; line speed and changeover decisions were the production manager's, recorded against my shift record.
Wrote the shift's open items and hand-over conditions on the hand-over sheet for the next supervisor.
Work sample: one week's briefing records with the crew leads' signatures, the stoppage log for the same week and one hand-over sheet, with the line system references as a verification trail.

Interviewer 2 note: asked to run a shift-start briefing for the panel, the candidate covered the line allocation, the two safety notices, the changeover time and the target for each line in that order, asked each crew lead by name to confirm their allocation, and finished inside the five minutes the standard allows.

Reference call with the former production manager: confirmed the candidate ran the shift and the briefings in the period, that line speed decisions stayed with the manager, and confirmed the employment dates.

propositions.text: The candidate allocated a crew of seventeen across a bottling plant's three high-speed lines each shift for four years under the plant's crewing plan, and resolved line stoppages with the shift maintenance technician under the stoppage procedure with each stoppage logged in the line system.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the stoppage log document the crewing and the stoppage handling.

propositions.rationale: The resume, the briefing records and the reference call document the briefings and the decision boundary.

gold.expectedGap: Hand-over conditions are documented on the hand-over sheet for the next supervisor, but the sheet's open items section is not audited in the materials.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Record the interview observation as what was observed in one exercise; do not extend it into a general judgement of the candidate beyond that observation.
followUpTargets: Ask whether the hand-over sheet's open items were reviewed by the production manager and how often.
